## 01. Launching Brand

### Situation

A new brand, product, campaign, or service is preparing to meet the market for the first time.

### Goals

- Make the first impression clear.
- Explain the brand quickly.
- Launch with a site or app that feels ownable.
- Avoid looking like a template.

### Fears

- The launch feels forgettable.
- The web presence cannot explain the brand.
- The site looks finished but not meaningful.

### Language That Resonates

- first screen
- launch
- starting point
- clear brand sentence
- designed to be remembered

### Avoid

- mature-operation language too early
- complex maintenance talk
- vague future language

### Usually Needs

WEB, BRANDING, UI/UX

## 02. Repositioning Brand

### Situation

An existing brand has a site or identity, but it no longer matches the business, audience, or ambition.

### Goals

- Reframe how the market sees the brand.
- Replace generic visuals and copy.
- Create a stronger digital identity.
- Make the brand feel more focused and credible.

- The renewal looks like a surface refresh.
- The team loses what already works.
- The new site feels different but not clearer.

### Language That Resonates

- redefine
- structure
- standard
- reason to choose
- not decoration
- web as proof

WEB, BRANDING, UI/UX, SEO STRATEGY

WE BUILD THE ROUTE." 등).

다만 **세일즈·제안 단계에서 쓰이는 두 보조 문서**에서 동반자 컨셉이 옅어집니다.

# Positioning

Use this file when writing why NINEONELABS should be chosen over another option.

## Core Position

NINEONELABS is for brands that need a digital experience built around identity, interaction, and proof. We are not the cheapest production option and not a slow corporate agency. We are the crew that turns undefined brand ambition into a working web/app/brand system.

## Versus Cheaper Freelancer

### What They Offer

- lower cost
- fast production
- narrower execution

### Where They Fail

- strategy, brand, UI/UX, and engineering often split apart
- long-term operation may be unsupported
- identity can become template-like

### NINEONELABS Position

# Client Archetypes

Use this file to avoid generic `your brand` copy. The client is the main character, but the client is not always in the same situation.

## 01. Launching Brand

### Situation

A new brand, product, campaign, or service is preparing to meet the market for the first time.

### Goals

- Make the first impression clear.
- Explain the brand quickly.
- Launch with a site or app that feels ownable.
- Avoid looking like a template.

### Fears

- The launch feels forgettable.
- The web presence cannot explain the brand.
- The site looks finished but not meaningful.

### Language That Resonates

- first screen
- launch
- starting point
- clear brand sentence
- designed to be remembered

### Avoid

- mature-operation language too early
- complex maintenance talk
- vague future language

### Usually Needs

WEB, BRANDING, UI/UX

## 02. Repositioning Brand

### Situation

An existing brand has a site or identity, but it no longer matches the business, audience, or ambition.

### Goals

- Reframe how the market sees the brand.
- Replace generic visuals and copy.
- Create a stronger digital identity.
- Make the brand feel more focused and credible.

### Fears

- The renewal looks like a surface refresh.
- The team loses what already works.
- The new site feels different but not clearer.

### Language That Resonates

- redefine
- structure
- standard
- reason to choose
- not decoration
- web as proof

### Avoid

- `new look` as the main promise
- trend-led design language
- dismissing the existing brand history

### Usually Needs

WEB, BRANDING, UI/UX, SEO STRATEGY

## 03. Operating Brand

### Situation

A brand already has a working digital presence, but it needs stability, content control, performance, and ongoing improvement.

### Goals

- Keep the site stable.
- Improve performance and usability.
- Update content without friction.
- Build a system that can grow.

### Fears

- Launch partner disappears after handoff.
- Small fixes become slow or expensive.
- Content cannot be updated easily.
- Growth breaks the structure.

### Language That Resonates

- orbit
- system
- maintenance
- CMS control
- iteration
- stable operation

### Avoid

- overly poetic launch language
- one-time project framing
- technical jargon without business impact

### Usually Needs

MAINTENANCE, CMS SYSTEM, UI/UX, WEB

## Archetype Use Rules

- Do not mention the archetype name in public copy unless it is useful.
- Use archetypes to choose the angle, not to label the client.
- If copy feels generic, identify the archetype before rewriting.
- When multiple archetypes apply, prioritize the one that matches the current section's job.

# Client Archetypes

Use this file to avoid generic `your brand` copy. The client is the main character, but the client is not always in the same situation.

## 01. Launching Brand

### Situation

A new brand, product, campaign, or service is preparing to meet the market for the first time.

### Goals

- Make the first impression clear.
- Explain the brand quickly.
- Launch with a site or app that feels ownable.
- Avoid looking like a template.

### Fears

- The launch feels forgettable.
- The web presence cannot explain the brand.
- The site looks finished but not meaningful.

### Language That Resonates

- first screen
- launch
- starting point
- clear brand sentence
- designed to be remembered
- 함께 시작
- 첫 여정

### Avoid

- mature-operation language too early
- complex maintenance talk
- vague future language

### Companion Stance

- 첫 발걸음을 함께 떼는 crew — 브랜드의 첫 화면과 구조를 같이 설계한다.
- 방향이 흔들릴 때 기준선을 잡아주는 조력자.
- 출시 이후에도 같은 자리에서 다음 단계를 준비한다.

### Usually Needs

WEB, BRANDING, UI/UX

## 02. Repositioning Brand

### Situation

An existing brand has a site or identity, but it no longer matches the business, audience, or ambition.

### Goals

- Reframe how the market sees the brand.
- Replace generic visuals and copy.
- Create a stronger digital identity.
- Make the brand feel more focused and credible.

### Fears

- The renewal looks like a surface refresh.
- The team loses what already works.
- The new site feels different but not clearer.

### Language That Resonates

- redefine
- structure
- standard
- reason to choose
- not decoration
- web as proof

### Avoid

- `new look` as the main promise
- trend-led design language
- dismissing the existing brand history

### Usually Needs

WEB, BRANDING, UI/UX, SEO STRATEGY

## 03. Operating Brand

### Situation

A brand already has a working digital presence, but it needs stability, content control, performance, and ongoing improvement.

### Goals

- Keep the site stable.
- Improve performance and usability.
- Update content without friction.
- Build a system that can grow.

### Fears

- Launch partner disappears after handoff.
- Small fixes become slow or expensive.
- Content cannot be updated easily.
- Growth breaks the structure.

### Language That Resonates

- orbit
- system
- maintenance
- CMS control
- iteration
- stable operation

### Avoid

- overly poetic launch language
- one-time project framing
- technical jargon without business impact

### Usually Needs

MAINTENANCE, CMS SYSTEM, UI/UX, WEB

## Archetype Use Rules

- Do not mention the archetype name in public copy unless it is useful.
- Use archetypes to choose the angle, not to label the client.

# Client Archetypes

Use this file to avoid generic `your brand` copy. The client is the main character, but the client is not always in the same situation.

## 01. Launching Brand

### Situation

A new brand, product, campaign, or service is preparing to meet the market for the first time.

### Goals

- Make the first impression clear.
- Explain the brand quickly.
- Launch with a site or app that feels ownable.
- Avoid looking like a template.

### Fears

- The launch feels forgettable.
- The web presence cannot explain the brand.
- The site looks finished but not meaningful.

### Language That Resonates

- first screen
- launch
- starting point
- clear brand sentence
- designed to be remembered
- 함께 시작
- 첫 여정

### Avoid

- mature-operation language too early
- complex maintenance talk
- vague future language

### Companion Stance

- 첫 발걸음을 함께 떼는 crew — 브랜드의 첫 화면과 구조를 같이 설계한다.
- 방향이 흔들릴 때 기준선을 잡아주는 조력자.
- 출시 이후에도 같은 자리에서 다음 단계를 준비한다.

### Usually Needs

WEB, BRANDING, UI/UX

## 02. Repositioning Brand

### Situation

An existing brand has a site or identity, but it no longer matches the business, audience, or ambition.

### Goals

- Reframe how the market sees the brand.
- Replace generic visuals and copy.
- Create a stronger digital identity.
- Make the brand feel more focused and credible.

### Fears

- The renewal looks like a surface refresh.
- The team loses what already works.
- The new site feels different but not clearer.

### Language That Resonates

- redefine
- structure
- standard
- reason to choose
- not decoration
- web as proof
- 다음 여정
- 방향을 다시 잡다

### Avoid

- `new look` as the main promise
- trend-led design language
- dismissing the existing brand history

### Companion Stance

- 기존 경로를 함께 점검하는 navigator — 무엇을 남기고 무엇을 바꿀지 같이 결정한다.
- 브랜드의 다음 여정을 웹 구조와 카피로 다시 그린다.
- 새로움을 위한 새로움이 아니라, 더 명확한 방향으로 안내한다.

### Usually Needs

WEB, BRANDING, UI/UX, SEO STRATEGY

## 03. Operating Brand

### Situation

A brand already has a working digital presence, but it needs stability, content control, performance, and ongoing improvement.

### Goals

- Keep the site stable.
- Improve performance and usability.
- Update content without friction.
- Build a system that can grow.

### Fears

- Launch partner disappears after handoff.
- Small fixes become slow or expensive.
- Content cannot be updated easily.
- Growth breaks the structure.

### Language That Resonates

- orbit
- system
- maintenance
- CMS control
- iteration
- stable operation
- 함께 머무르다
- 궤도를 함께 돌다

### Avoid

- overly poetic launch language
- one-time project framing
- technical jargon without business impact

### Companion Stance

- 궤도를 같이 도는 운영 파트너 — 런칭 이후에도 시스템 옆에 머문다.
- 작은 이슈를 빠르게 해결하고, CMS와 콘텐츠를 함께 운영한다.
- 성장의 속도에 맞춰 구조를 같이 확장한다.

### Usually Needs

MAINTENANCE, CMS SYSTEM, UI/UX, WEB

## Archetype Use Rules

- Do not mention the archetype name in public copy unless it is useful.
- Use archetypes to choose the angle, not to label the client.
- If copy feels generic, identify the archetype before rewriting.
- When multiple archetypes apply, prioritize the one that matches the current section's job.

다만 서비스 섹션은 구체적인 톤이어야 하고, voice.md에서 "브랜드 톤만 — 기능이나 결과물로 리드. 구체적인 도구, 산출물, 또는 증거 필요"라고 했으니 여기에 "궤도"를 추가하면 톤 규칙을 깰 수 있다. 더 신중하게 접근해야겠다.

다시 생각해보니 현재 유지보수 카피 "런칭 이후에도 시스템은 계속 움직여야 합니다"는 명확하고 강력하고, "함께 관리합니다"에 동반자 언어가 포함되어 있으니 이 정도면 충분하다.

사용자 관점에서 실질적으로 접근해보자. 사용자가 "변경해야할 부분이 있다면 이를 최적화해줘. 문맥상 이상하지 않도록"이라고 요청했으니, 이 기준에 맞춰 검토해야 한다.

지금 정말 바꿔야 할 부분은 introAction beat 2의 관점 불일치다. Beat 1은 "우리와 클라이언트" 관점인데 beat 2는 "제품과 최종 사용자"로 넘어가면서 미묘한 POV 시프트가 생긴다. 이걸 더 타이트하게 정렬해야 한다.

Beat 1을 다시 보면 "WE START BESIDE YOU"와 "같은 자리에서 방향을 맞춥니다"는 우리 주체로 일관되는데, Beat 2의 "READY TO LAUNCH"는 이 흐름을 끊고 있다.

실제로는 이 POV 시프트가 의도적일 수도 있다. "우리가 정렬한다 → 시스템이 준비된다 → 런칭된다"는 호는 beat 2에서 최종 사용자 관점으로 전환되면서 공동 작업의 결과를 보여주는 거다. 하지만 "사용자는 다음 장면으로 들어옵니다"는 이미 구축된 사이트에서의 사용자 행동을 설명하는 거라 독자(잠재 클라이언트)가 혼란스러워할 수 있다. 어떤 사용자를 말하는 건지, 내 사용자인지 내가 방문자로서의 사용자인지 불명확하다.

beat 2를 런칭 후 사용자 행동이 아니라 런칭으로 이어지는 공동 노력을 설명하도록 다시 쓰면 더 명확할 것 같다. 예를 들어 "구조가 잡히면, 브랜드는 첫 목소리를 냅니다. 함께 쌓은 모든 결정이 화면 위에서 보이기 시작합니다"처럼 말이다. 하지만 시각적 맥락에서 "정적인 시작에서 움직임이 생기며 런치 시퀀스가 시작된다"고 했으니, 이건 런칭 시퀀스를 시각적으로 표현하는 거고, 카피는 런칭할 때 일어나는 일을 설명해야 한다.
